composition_parti.rule_append: There is no module and no bay system; the design is controlled by keeping one material unbroken over an irregular volume, and by making the roof large and simple enough to gather that volume into one shape.

variants.note: The long rear catslide, taken from seventeenth-century New England to bring the roof to the ground.

roof_form.rule: A broad sheltering roof of large simple planes, often gambrel or a long sweeping gable, coming low to the ground; the largest single plane not less than 40 percent of total roof area.

eave_condition.rule: Eave overhang shall not exceed 12 in and rake overhang shall not exceed 10 in, both closed tight to the wall plane with no exposed brackets, rafter tails, or purlin ends.

gable_treatment.rule: Shingle exposure is uniform over the entire building; decorative butt patterning, where used at all, shall not exceed 10 percent of total wall area and shall occur only within a single gable field.

primary_cladding.rule: The shingle field shall be continuous across every storey line, corner, and change of plane on all elevations. This single rule is what separates the style from Queen Anne and admits no exceptions.

secondary_cladding.rule: No second cladding material may interrupt the continuous shingle field.

material_change_rule.rule: The shingle field is continuous across every storey line, corner, and change of plane; the sole permitted material change is a rock-faced masonry base terminating at or below the first-floor sill line.

variants.note: A Richardson-derived signature: the base terminates at or below the first-floor window sill line and is the only material change permitted on the elevation.

foundation_expression.rule: Where a masonry base is used it shall be rock-faced, shall terminate at or below the first-floor window sill line, and shall be the only material change permitted on the elevation.

water_table.rule: No water table may interrupt the shingle field.

belt_course.rule: No belt or storey band may interrupt the shingle field.

corner_board.rule: No corner board may interrupt the shingle field; the shingles wrap the corner. A corner board is the single diagnostic tell that moves a building to Queen Anne.

expressed_frame.rule: 'Eave overhang shall not exceed 12 in and rake overhang shall not exceed 10 in, and both shall be closed tight to the wall plane with no exposed bracke[ts].' The style's whole argument is a continuous skin, and an expressed member would interrupt it -- which is why it is forbidden here and required by its Stick Style predecessor.

variants.note: `member_status` at ontology 0.7.0 (OQ 47). Categorical, so it is a variant rather than a parameter -- it carries no unit and the kit checker is right to insist that a parameter does.

frieze.rule: No frieze board may interrupt the shingle field.

lite_pattern.note: Multi-light upper sash over single-light lower, a documented late-19th-century pattern.

variants.note: c03: projecting hoods, crowns, pedimented heads, and moulded sills are prohibited.

window_surround_wood.rule: Window and door casing shall not exceed 3 in in width and shall not project more than 1 in from the shingle plane.

window_grouping_rule.rule: Horizontal window bands of multiple sash grouped under a single head, separated by long stretches of plain shingle; the rhythm belongs to the openings, not to a structural bay.

variants.note: A subordinate volume pulled under the house's own skin and linked by a low shingled hyphen the main roof sweeps down over -- the catslide move the saltbox affinity already uses to bring the roof to the ground. This style unifies its massing by the surface rather than by articulation, so it can absorb an extra volume more cheaply than any other style in the corpus: the shingle field simply continues across it.

Standing free on the lot in the same skin, the same shallow tight-cut eave and the same plain butt. Correct where the lot has a service drive, but it gives up the one thing the attached version buys -- a single continuously modelled mass.

c01 admits no exceptions: the shingle field runs across every storey line, corner and change of plane, with no corner board, water table, belt course or frieze board interrupting it. A garage given corner boards and a cased door is the exact move that makes a Shingle Style house a Queen Anne one (diagnostic tell 1), and it does it at the largest opening on the building.

c03 prohibits projecting hoods, crowns, pedimented heads and moulded sills and caps casing at 3 in. The vehicle opening reads as punched into the shingle field like every other opening, or it does not belong to this style.

The principal elevation's large openings are voids carved out of the volume -- porches and loggias, and horizontal bands of sash under one head. A pair of vehicle doors is an applied plane of moving hardware that cannot read as a carved void, and its width has no relative anywhere in the window banding. Turn them onto a flank or a court, per groupings/garage-and-hyphen.json.

cladding_continuity.value: one shingle field, unbroken from the house across the hyphen and around all four sides of the garage volume, at the same exposure
cladding_continuity.note: The rule is the style's own and is retrieved; extending it over a volume the style never built is the authored part. It is also what makes the strategy work -- an absorbed garage is invisible in a way it can never be in a trimmed style.

shingle_exposure.note: Same exposure on the garage as on the house; a coarser shingle on the outbuilding is the commonest way the field stops reading as one surface.

max_casing_width.note: Applies to the vehicle door as to every other opening, which in practice means no surround at all.

max_eave_projection.note: The garage and the hyphen carry the same shallow tight-cut eave; a deeper overhang over the bays is the giveaway that the volume was designed separately.

max_door_width.note: Two openings with a shingled pier between them. Beyond about 10 ft there is too little field left between jamb and corner for the surface to read as continuous, which is the whole strategy. OQ 18, 24 Aug 2026: reclassified from `editorial` to `invented`. The two are different claims -- the schema defines editorial as 'our considered convention' and invented as 'no precedent exists' -- and `garage_strategy`'s own ontology note says in its first sentence that no historical precedent exists. A number about the garage door itself cannot be a convention drawn from tradition, because the tradition has no garage. The parameters left editorial on this slot are the ones carried from the dependency tradition rather than invented for the garage: subordination, ridge ratio, pitch match, cladding continuity.

hyphen_length.note: Taken unchanged from the grouping, which takes it in turn from dependency-and-hyphen. Here the link is shingled and roofed by the main roof continuing down over it, so it reads as modelling rather than as a connector.

garage_strategy.rule: No traditional precedent exists; the garage is authored as one more freely modelled volume pulled under the house's own continuous shingle field, joined by a low hyphen the main roof sweeps down over, because this style is unified by its skin rather than by its articulation and can therefore absorb a subordinate volume at no cost to the composition -- while a garage given its own corner boards, casing or eave breaks c01, the one rule the style has that admits no exceptions.

edit_provenance.note: Specified rather than extended: the inherited answer reaching this node from queen-anne-british is an informal gabled outbuilding 'in the same red-brick-and-tile-hanging vocabulary as the house', which is Old English and not this style's vocabulary at all. The structural idea behind it -- one more informally massed volume, never centred on the composed front -- survives; the materials and the trim do not.

sources: Authored, not retrieved. There is no historical precedent for a garage in this or any traditional style (docs/inheritance.md).
